point_walk.detail: driver evidence/p256_point_walk_test.c runs the shipped counted step on real P-256 points, but its driver-side table construction still disagrees with the bigint oracle at row 3 of 2048, so no point-walk PASS is claimed in this revision; the kernel test of record remains the field-primitive test (0/10,770).

record_pipeline.detection: mix64(x3[0] ^ DPSALT) & ((1<<61)-1) == 0, executed inside the counted step (evidence/step_v10f_o3.c:71-72, rows mix_key+control in stepcount.json)
record_pipeline.recovery: pairwise key match on the sparse record key, solve x = (a-a2)/(b-b2) mod r, verify by recomputing [x]P and comparing the full point (census_v10f41.c:355-372)
record_pipeline.schedule: per round of n walkers: forward pre-products (n-1 muls), ONE fe_inv of the product, back-substitution (n-1 muls + n-1 muls) = 3(n-1) muls + 1 inv; each walker keeps 1/d_i and forms lambda = num_i * inv_i (already inside the counted step's 6-mul schedule), so the marginal charge is inv_ir/n per step.

storage.record_layout: x (32 B, full P-256 coordinate) + (a,b) coefficient pair (32 B packed) + 8 B tag/owner word
storage.why_sparse: dense records at S = 2^127.63 steps would need 2^61.17 B against the 2^73 B cap, so the sparse DP predicate is a DESIGN NECESSITY, not a saving; the dense every-step configuration is the census instrument only, and arm B measures the sparse pipeline.
